text:
anya: quick heads-up — landed the bulk of the docs split PRs this morning. they’re split across ~12 PRs (snippets, redirects, tocs, examples). we need a merge choreography so previews and redirects don’t break prod links
kevin: thanks for the heads-up. any failing previews right now?
sarah: saw one preview fail with `Broken anchor: #getting-started-quickstart` coming from the TOC update PR (PR 412). stack trace in the preview log points to the moved file names
docs-bot: PR #398 (snippets/cleanup) preview built: success :white_check_mark:
oliver: i can take redirects (PR 405) but we should not merge redirects before anchor fixes — redirects will 301 to anchors that might not exist yet
anya: agreed. proposed order: 1) anchor/fragment fixes (small PRs that update anchors inside moved pages), 2) snippets and example imports (safe, non-link-changing), 3) redirects + canonical metadata, 4) TOC/top-level nav adjustments, 5) polish PRs. thoughts?
kevin: +1. also: CI previews are flakey when we trigger 10+ builds at once. can we throttle or batch? maybe use a single meta-branch to consolidate preview-run the big merge window
sarah: we tried the meta-branch for the last migration and it reduced preview noise. downside: harder to roll back a single doc PR. but for this scale it’s fine
lia: can we add a small check in docs CI that ensures `anchors.md` contains any anchor referenced by a redirect? pseudo-check: ```bash
# run in docs CI
for a in $(grep -oP '#\K[\w-]+' redirects.yaml); do
  grep -R --quiet "#${a}" docs || echo "missing anchor: ${a}" && exit 1
done
```
anya: i like that. short-term we do manual order + reviewers, long-term add the script
kevin: reviewers — assign: me -> snippets (PR 398, 421), sarah -> anchors (PR 412, 419), oliver -> redirects (PR 405). anya will approve TOC (PR 430). can we add `docs/preview-needed` label to the small anchor fixes to get quick rebuilds?
sarah: added labels to 412 & 419. re-run preview for 412 now?
docs-bot: rebuild triggered for PR 412 by @sarah — preview URL: https://preview.docs.redwood-inference.com/pr-412 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin: small nit — one snippet file imports `from redwood import Client` but our python sdk is `redwood_inference`. i left a suggestion on PR 398. will fix and push in branch
anya: merge window suggestion: tomorrow 09:00-11:00 PT. during that time we serial-merge in this order: anchors -> snippets -> redirects -> tocs. everyone available for quick revert if something goes sideways?
oliver: i’ll be online. will watch redirects closely and have the rollback redirect rules ready
sarah: i’ll stay on-call for the anchor merges. if preview shows a missing anchor, hold merges and i’ll patch
docs-bot: PR #412 preview failed: Broken anchor detected in `getting-started.md:line 124` :warning:
kevin: copying error — looks like the `#quickstart-setup` anchor changed to `#quick-start-setup` during move. small fix incoming
kevin: pushed fix to PR 419 (anchor-normalize). requesting review from @sarah
sarah: reviewed and approved, re-triggering preview. :eyes:
docs-bot: PR #419 preview built: success. :white_check_mark:
anya: okay once 419 is green i’ll merge it then we can merge snippets (398). remember to add the `docs/no-preview` label to bulk merges if we’re doing a consolidated meta-branch; otherwise keep previews enabled for safety
oliver: question for product: should redirects include historical slugs for older blog posts? that’s separate but we can tack it into PR 405 if low risk
anya: let’s keep redirects PR minimal — canonical redirects only. historical slugs can be a follow-up once site is stable
kevin: merging PR 398 now (snippets). tagging @anya to watch console for broken examples
anya: merged. docs-bot: PR #398 merged by @kevin at 1781234660 :rocket:
sarah: quick sanity check on prod staging: `curl -I https://docs.redwood-inference.com/sdk/python#quick-start-setup` -> 200 + correct redirect to new page
lia: after redirects are merged, i’ll run a full link-check pass (linkinator) before TOC change
anya: great — final ask: please add `docs/split-migration` to PRs you open for follow-ups so we can track the backlog. thanks everyone, huge help :tada:
